definition: PyArrow is the Python library for Apache Arrow, a columnar in-memory format for moving data between tools without copying.
details: Apache Arrow was co-created by Wes McKinney and others in 2016 and is developed under the Apache Software Foundation.

explainer.lead: How to install PyArrow, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Apache Software Foundation (Apache Arrow project), co-created by Wes McKinney.

quickstart.python:
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

table = pa.table({"text": ["hi", "bye"], "label": [1, 0]})
pq.write_table(table, "data.parquet")
print(pq.read_table("data.parquet").to_pandas())

explainer.inAi: Hugging Face Datasets, Polars and DuckDB all store data as Arrow, so Parquet/Arrow files are the common currency for training data.
